summary: Di Luo is a scholar in Sinology, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies. Luo earned a PhD from the University of Southern California (attested 2016), supervised by Dominic Cheung, Sonya S. Lee, and Bettine Birge, following MA supervision by James Steele.

Diana L. Eck is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. She earned degrees from Smith College, SOAS, and Harvard University under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. Eck was appointed a professor at Harvard University around 1976.

Diana Lange works in Tibetology, Sinology, and Central Asian studies. Educated at Leipzig, Tibet, and Humboldt universities and the EPHE, she held posts at Humboldt, Leipzig, Zurich, and Hamburg before becoming Central Asian professor at Humboldt in 2025.

Diane A. Lichtenstein earned a PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1977. By 2005, she held posts as Adjunct Professor of Anthropology at both Baldwin Wallace University and the Cleveland Institute of Art.

Diane E. Riggs specializes in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She earned her PhD at UCLA in 2010 under William M. Bodiford and Myōsei Tatsuguchi, later teaching at Kenyon College, Pepperdine University, and Western Michigan University.
Diane L. Howard is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who studied as a graduate student at McMaster University under the supervision of Graeme MacQueen (attested 1982).
Dickwela Piyananda is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. Piyananda earned a PhD from the Catholic University of America under the doctoral supervision of Siegfried A. Schulz.
Diego Loukota is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed an MA at Peking University and earned a PhD from the University of California, Los Angeles, in 2019.

Dieter B. Kapp (1941–2021) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Heidelberg under Hermann Berger (Dr. phil. 1971). He held positions at Heidelberg and served as director of the Indology and Tamilistics institute at Cologne (1990–2006).
Dieter George (1935–1985) was an Indologist who served at the Prussian State Library from around 1972 until 1985, succeeding Wolfgang Voigt.

Dieter Schlingloff is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his doctorate at Göttingen and habilitation at Humboldt University. He served as a professor at Kiel University (1968–1971) and at the University of Munich (1972–1996).

Dieter Schuh is a Tibetologist who studied at Cologne and Bonn. He served as professor of Tibetology at the University of Bonn (1978–2007) and founded the International Institute for Tibetan and Buddhist Studies, becoming its managing director around 2007.

Dietmar Rothermund (1933–2020) was a historian and Indologist who earned his PhD from the University of Pennsylvania (1959). He served at Heidelberg University as Wissenschaftlicher Assistent in 1963 and as Chair of South Asian History (1968–2001).

Dilgo Khyentse (1910–1991) was a master of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Shechen Gyaltsap Pema Namgyal and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, subsequently teaching figures including Chögyam Trungpa, Matthieu Ricard, and Sogyal Rinpoche.

Dilip K. Chakrabarti is a scholar of Indology and archaeology who studied at the University of Calcutta. He taught at Calcutta (1965–1977), Delhi (1977–1990), and was Professor of South Asian Archaeology at the University of Cambridge (1990–2008).

Dilip Kumar Biswas (1920–2003) was a scholar in Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Presidency University and the University of Calcutta under Prabodh Chandra Bagchi, and he later held posts at Visva-Bharati University and Calcutta.

Dilli Raman Regmi (1914–2001) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Madras and earned a D. Litt. at Patna University in 1961, and he taught at Mahatma Gandhi Kashi Vidyapith.

Dina Bangdel (1964–2017) was a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She held academic posts at Ohio State University (ca. 2002–2007) and Virginia Commonwealth University (ca. 2007–2017).

Dines Andersen (1861–1940) was a Danish Indologist and linguist. He studied at the University of Copenhagen under Michael Viggo Fausbøll, Vilhelm Thomsen, and Karl Verner, later serving there as professor of Indian philology from 1903 to 1927.

Dineschandra Sircar (1907–1985) was an Indian epigraphist and historian. He served as Government Epigraphist for India, taught as a lecturer at the University of Calcutta starting in 1937, and became its Carmichael Professor of Ancient Indian History in 1962.
